ana: Quick thread 90min ticket: refreshing the Web Hello quickstart (Docker + auth + CI). Found three recurring issues from support tickets: hardcoded API keys in examples, a Dockerfile that starts the app as root, and no GH Actions example showing how to wire secrets securely. I'll open a small PR to fix snippets, add a short troubleshooting section, and include a one-line migration hint for SDK v4->v6.
ben: Thanks. Can you also add an example of DefaultCredentials fallback for local dev? Folks copy `const API_KEY = 'sk_...'` into repos.
nana: (typo) I meant ana — yes. Plan is to replace that with: 
```js
// prefer DefaultCredentials: env -> file -> interactive
const creds = await DefaultCredentials.load();
const client = new RedwoodClient({ auth: creds });
```
ryn: For Dockerfile, change request: build as root for layers, but run as non-root user. Add HEALTHCHECK and switch to `npm ci` for reproducible builds. Also include a note about not mounting secrets in the image.
nana: Will do. Proposed Dockerfile snippet in the PR: 
```dockerfile
FROM node:18-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production
COPY . .
RUN addgroup -S app && adduser -S app -G app && chown -R app:app /app
USER app
EXPOSE 3000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s CMD curl -f http://localhost:3000/health || exit 1
CMD ["node","server.js"]
```
sam: Nice. Please also add a tiny GH Actions snippet showing how to set REDWOOD_API_KEY via repo secrets instead of hardcoding. Something like: 
```yaml
- name: Set REDWOOD_API_KEY
  run: echo "REDWOOD_API_KEY=${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
```
ryn: And add a brief `:no_entry_sign:` warning under the code sample: "Never commit API keys or print tokens in logs." That would reduce noisy support tickets.
ben: On the docs site preview, the CORS section is missing the `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` callout. For local dev with cookies we should show the fetch usage: `fetch(url, { credentials: 'include' })`.
nana: Adding a short troubleshooting list:
- Ensure Access-Control-Allow-Origin matches the origin (or use `*` only for public endpoints)
- Set Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true when sending cookies
- Use `fetch(..., { credentials: 'include' })` or axios `withCredentials: true`
- Check that redirects don't strip Authorization header
ryn: One more: migration hint for SDK v4 -> v6 (single line): update package, replace `new Client(opts)` with `new RedwoodClient({ auth })`, and confirm token retrieval method name change. Link to changelog.
ci-bot: Draft PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/619-web-hello-docker-auth-refresh 9checks queued: markdown-lint, link-check, sample-runner.
sam: I'll run the site preview and do a quick copyedit (tone + accessibility). If the GH Actions fenced block renders strangely, change the fence to `yaml`.
nana: Thanks! If CI is green I'll ask for a quick approve and land in the next docs patch. We'll add one-line CHANGELOG entry: "web quickstart: Docker non-root, CI secrets example, auth snippet cleanup, CORS troubleshooting"
ben: Sounds good. I'll also open a small follow-up issue to add a short FAQ about local dev auth edge cases.
nana: Closing loop here. Thanks all :tada:
